full_judgment:
2. Plaintiff-appellant filed other Suit No. 241 of 1964 in the Court of Munsiff, Cox's Bazar, for redemption of the suit land which was transferred by him to the defendant-respondent under a registered instrument dated 11 November, 1953. He claimed that the transaction in question was a Kot-mortgage and that the entire consideration for the mortgage was satisfied by usufructs of the land during this period of about 11 years. The defendant contested the suit taking the ground that the transaction was an out and out sale with a condition for reconveyance on repayment of the consideration within a period of 5 years but no repayment having been made within the stipulated period the transaction of sale became absolute and as such the plaintiff was not entitled to any decree for redemption or reconveyance. The trial court held that the transaction was an out and out sale and dismissed the suit. But on appeal the learned Subordinate Judge reversed trial court's finding and found the transaction to be a complete unufructuary mortgage the consideration of which was already satisfied by the usufructs of the land, and on such finding, decreed the suit for redemption: Defendant preferred a second appeal (S.A. No. 648 of 1967) and the High Court Division reversed the finding of the lower appellate court and held that the transaction was an out and out sale. The High Court Division then relying upon a decision of this Division in Civil Appeals Nos. 31-77 of 1974 held that the transaction was 'past and closed' and as such it could not be a unufructuary mortgage within the meaning of the President's Order No. 88 of 1972 which amended section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950. In this view of the matter, the High Court Division found the suit barred by limitation as well as by the doctrine of "transaction past and closed", set aside the judgment of the lower appellate court and restored that of the trial court. 

 5. But on perusal of the judgment of the High Court Division it is found that learned Advocates of both the parties who appeared there were confused between the period of subsistence of a usufructuary mortgage and the period of limitation in the case of a suit for redemption of a mortgaged land, The Maximum period for which a usufructuary mortgage can be entered into was fifteen years under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1950, But by Ordinance No. XXI of 1969, section 95 was amended and thereby the maximum period for a usufructuary mortgage was reduced to seven years. And unless earlier redeemed by repayment of the consideration a mortgagor acquires right to redemption on the expiry of the maximum period of seven years, and if the mortgage does not voluntarily restore possession of the land to the mortgagor, the latter may file a suit for redemption within a period of 60 years from the date of accrual of his right of redemption. In this case the suit was filed just on the accrual of the right of redemption and as such it is not barred by limitation.
